whatIsIt.eli5: A team that keeps every helper's work: notes go through two helper groups one after the other, and all piles are joined at the end.
whatIsIt.simple: YOLOv9's main block (the GELAN idea). It splits the input, sends one part through two stages (each: a RepCSP block then a 3×3 Conv), and joins the two original halves with both stage outputs.
whatIsIt.engineer: cv1 (1×1, c3) → chunk(2) → cv2 = Seq(RepCSP(c3/2→c4, n), Conv3×3) → cv3 = Seq(RepCSP(c4, n), Conv3×3) → cat[c3/2, c3/2, c4, c4] → cv4 (1×1, c2).

whyExists.eli5: Saving every step's work helps learning and keeps details.
whyExists.simple: Generalized ELAN: aggregating outputs from several depths gives a rich mix of features and good gradient paths, and any block can be plugged in (here RepCSP).
whyExists.engineer: GELAN (paper §4.2): ELAN-style aggregation generalised to arbitrary computational blocks for parameter efficiency.

eli5: Pass one pile through two helper groups.
simple: cv1 (1×1) to c3 channels, split in half.
Join both halves and both stage outputs; cv4 (1×1).
engineer: RepCSP = C3 with RepBottlenecks (RepConv 3×3 + 1×1 branches, fused at export).

example.eli5: YOLOv9t layer 4 works on an 80×80 picture.
example.simple: YOLOv9t layer 4: 64 channels at 80×80, c3 = 64, c4 = 32, n = 1 (3 × depth), 65,216 parameters.
